Done. The solution is written to `/workspace/solution.md`, backed by a runnable, verified Go reference implementation at `/workspace/canopy-gateway-fix/`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** the gateway's default registry path was a fixed `runs.jsonl`. Every instance used the same file, so a scratch/secondary gateway on any non-default port read and wrote the canonical `:8091` live stack registry.

**Fix (in `state.go`):**
- `DefaultStateFile(addr)` parses the bind address and derives `<stateDir>/runs-<port>.jsonl` — distinct ports yield distinct files.
- `ResolveStateFile(addr)` returns `CANOPY_GATEWAY_STATE_FILE` **verbatim** when set, otherwise the derived path.
- `MigrateLegacyStateFile(addr)` is triple-gated: only when the port is the canonical `8091`, the derived target is absent, and no override is set. Scratch instances leave `runs.jsonl` untouched.

**Verification:** `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go test -v`, and `go test -race` all pass. Seven tests cover per-port derivation, verbatim override, the scratch-instance isolation regression, default-port-only migration, content preservation, no-clobber, and override skip. The exact observed output and a real-gateway regression checklist are included in the document.
